proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_not_eventually_constant :
    (∀ N : ℕ, ∃ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = true) ∧
      (∀ N : ℕ, ∃ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = false) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason:
The centre column takes both colours infinitely often. This is the period-1 case of Prize 1, proved outright: an eventually constant sequence is eventually periodic, so this is the smallest piece of the prize that can be closed today, and nothing on the board closes any piece of it. Both halves are contradictions against Jen's theorem, and neither needs anything unproved.

BLACK HALF. Suppose centerColumn t = true for every t ≥ N. `centerColumn_succ_of_black` at t says centerColumn (t + 1) = !evolve t (-1); the left side is true, so evolve t (-1) = false, for every t ≥ N. Column -1 is then constantly white from N and the centre column constantly black from N, so both are eventually periodic with period 1 — which `not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent (-1)` forbids. (That lemma's second column is `-1 + 1`, which needs one `norm_num` to be seen as 0, and centerColumn is `fun t => evolve t 0` definitionally.)

WHITE HALF. Suppose centerColumn t = false for every t ≥ N. `rule30_eq` at position 1 and time t reads evolve (t + 1) 1 = evolve t 0 XOR (evolve t 1 || evolve t 2), and evolve t 0 is false, so evolve (t + 1) 1 = (evolve t 1 || evolve t 2). Column 1 can therefore never turn from black to white after N. Two cases. If evolve t0 1 = true for some t0 ≥ N then evolve t 1 = true for every t ≥ t0 by induction, so columns 0 and 1 are both eventually periodic, contradicting `not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent 0`. Otherwise evolve t 1 = false for every t ≥ N, and then the same identity forces (evolve t 1 || evolve t 2) = false, so evolve t 2 = false for every t ≥ N too — columns 0 and 2 are both eventually periodic, contradicting `not_isEventuallyPeriodic_pair 0 2`.

Why a proof of the wall would cite it: the mask law and `centerColumn_periodic_damage_white` in this tier both reason about the centre column's white cells, and this is what says those cells exist at all. It is also the base case of the only ladder in the prize's direction that anyone can currently climb.
proposals.disclaims: This is the period-1 case of Prize 1 and nothing more. It says nothing about any period above 1, and no induction on the period is implied or available — the two halves use completely different arguments and neither generalises. It is not a step toward either P1 wall.

witness.expression: ((List.range 12).any (fun t => centerColumn t)) && ((List.range 12).any (fun t => ! centerColumn t))
witness.range: t < 12 — a finite shadow only. Both colours occurring among the first twelve cells is a necessary consequence of the statement, so this catches a flipped quantifier or a swapped true/false; it is NOT evidence for the infinitary claim, which no finite range can carry.

proposals.statement:
theorem column_neg_one_damage_mask (X Y : Config) (t : ℕ)
    (h0 : column X 0 t = column Y 0 t)
    (h1 : column X 0 (t + 1) = column Y 0 (t + 1)) :
    xor (column X (-1) t) (column Y (-1) t)
      = ((! column X 0 t) && xor (column X 1 t) (column Y 1 t)) := by
  sorry
proposals.disclaims: NOT a sufficient condition for the wall. It is unconditional and true of every pair of pictures, so it cannot by itself rule anything out; it is machinery a proof by contradiction would use, not an implication into the prize. It also says nothing about the white times, which is where the open part lives — it only says that at a white cell the mask is open.
proposals.reason:
Two pictures that agree at the origin at times t and t + 1 differ at column -1 at time t exactly where they differ at column 1 AND the shared origin cell is white. A black cell at the origin erases the difference; a white one passes it straight through.

WHY IT IS TRUE. `sideways_inverse` at position 0, applied to the row `evolveFrom X t`, says column X (-1) t = column X 0 (t + 1) XOR (column X 0 t || column X 1 t), and the same for Y. XOR the two equations. The h1 hypothesis cancels the first term outright. What is left is (a || b) XOR (a || b'), where a is the shared origin cell (by h0) and b, b' are the two column-1 cells: that is false when a is black and b XOR b' when a is white, which is exactly the right-hand side. A `cases` on a and on the two column-1 Booleans closes it; the only real step is aiming `sideways_inverse` at the right row, since `column X i t` is `evolveFrom X t i` and the lemma is stated about a bare `Config`.

WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT. Read it with X the seed and Y the picture grown from row p (`evolveFrom_evolve` identifies that with the seed's picture read p rows later). Then the hypotheses are exactly 'the centre column repeats at lag p at times t and t + 1', which is what the wall's hypothesis supplies, and the conclusion says: the failure of column -1 to repeat at lag p is the failure of column 1 to repeat at lag p, masked off at every black cell of the centre column. Jen's theorem forbids column 1 from repeating and forbids column -1 from repeating, and this identity is the only bridge on the board between those two facts. Any proof that a repeating centre column forces a repeating neighbour has to say what the mask does, and today nothing on the board says it.

witness.expression:
(List.range 12).all (fun v => ([1, 2] : List ℤ).all (fun f =>
  (List.range 9).all (fun t =>
    !(decide (column (fun i => decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3)) 0 t
        = column (fun i => xor (decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3))
            (decide (i = f))) 0 t) &&
      decide (column (fun i => decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3)) 0 (t + 1)
        = column (fun i => xor (decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3))
            (decide (i = f))) 0 (t + 1))) ||
    decide (xor (column (fun i => decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3)) (-1) t)
        (column (fun i => xor (decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3))
            (decide (i = f))) (-1) t)
      = ((! column (fun i => decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3)) 0 t) &&
          xor (column (fun i => decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3)) 1 t)
            (column (fun i => xor (decide ((i * i * i + (v : ℤ) * i + 1) % 7 < 3))
              (decide (i = f))) 1 t))))))
witness.range: twelve deterministic 'noisy' rows v < 12, each against itself with position f in {1, 2} flipped, at every t < 9. Evaluated true by `lake env lean` at seed time (explorer/seeder_p1_final.lean). NON-VACUITY CHECKED: within this exact range the left-hand side is genuinely nonzero at (v, f, t) = (0, 2, 6), (5, 1, 8), (5, 2, 7) and (7, 2, 6), so the witness exercises the branch that carries the content. The seed itself will not do here — its white left cone means a difference planted at position d takes about 4d rows to creep back to column 1, and over initialConfig with d ≤ 4 and t < 12 both sides are identically zero (explorer/seeder_p1_witness2.lean). Independently: 0 failures in 76,711 hypothesis hits over 400 random configuration pairs, 2,241 of them with a nonzero left-hand side (explorer/seeder_p1_damage.mjs).

proposals.statement:
theorem column_neg_two_damage_derivative (X Y : Config) (t : ℕ)
    (h0 : column X 0 t = column Y 0 t)
    (h1 : column X 0 (t + 1) = column Y 0 (t + 1)) :
    xor (column X (-2) t) (column Y (-2) t)
      = xor (xor (column X (-1) t) (column Y (-1) t))
          (xor (column X (-1) (t + 1)) (column Y (-1) (t + 1))) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason:
One column further left than the mask law, and there the mask disappears: the disagreement at column -2 is the plain discrete derivative of the disagreement at column -1. No masking, no `&&` — this is the one place in the leftward cascade where the relation is linear.

WHY IT IS TRUE. `sideways_inverse` at position -1 gives column X (-2) t = column X (-1) (t + 1) XOR (column X (-1) t || column X 0 t), and the same for Y. XOR the two. The bracket is (u || a) XOR (u' || a), where a is the shared origin cell by h0 and u, u' are the two column--1 cells: it is false when a is black and the column--1 disagreement when a is white. The two cases then join, and that is the whole trick: when a is black, `column_succ_of_black` applied to X and to Y (they share the origin cell at t by h0 and at t + 1 by h1) pins both column--1 cells to the complement of the same cell, so the column--1 disagreement is false there too. So in BOTH cases the bracket equals the column--1 disagreement at t, and the identity is the stated XOR of it with the one at t + 1.

WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT. Under a centre column repeating at lag p, it converts 'column -2 repeats at time t' into 'the column--1 mismatch is the same at t and t + 1'. So column -2 is eventually periodic exactly when the column--1 mismatch is eventually constant — and eventually constant means either eventually zero (column -1 repeats at lag p) or eventually one (column -1 repeats at lag 2p). Jen forbids both. That is a genuine structural fact about the assumed picture, in the same currency as the mask law and one column further in.
proposals.disclaims: The cascade does NOT continue, and this is the honest limit of the statement rather than a gap in it. The same claim one column further left — that the disagreement at -3 is the discrete derivative of the disagreement at -2 — is measured FALSE: 418 failures in 35,795 hypothesis hits over random configuration pairs (explorer/seeder_p1_damage.mjs). The reason is visible in the proof: at column -2 the second input to the `||` is still the shared origin column, and at -3 it is not. So a prover should not expect an induction here, and a seeder should not propose one.

proposals.statement:
theorem column_damage_zero_of_black_run (X Y : Config) (t j : ℕ)
    (hagree : ∀ s ≤ j, column X 0 (t + s) = column Y 0 (t + s))
    (hblack : ∀ s < j, column X 0 (t + s) = true)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ j) :
    column X (-(i : ℤ)) t = column Y (-(i : ℤ)) t := by
  sorry
proposals.reason:
A run of black cells in the shared centre column shields the left, one column per cell of the run. If two pictures have the same origin cell at times t .. t + j and that cell is black at t .. t + j - 1, then the two pictures agree at every position 0, -1, ..., -j at time t.

WHY IT IS TRUE. Write D i s for the disagreement between X and Y at position -i at time s, and prove by strong induction on i the triangle claim: D i s is false whenever t ≤ s and s + i ≤ t + j. At i = 0 that is hagree. At i = 1 it is `column_succ_of_black`, which at a black origin cell pins the cell at -1 to the complement of the origin cell one step later; both pictures have the same origin cell at s (hagree, since s ≤ t + j) and at s + 1 (hagree, since s + 1 ≤ t + j), and hblack applies because s - t < j. For the step, `sideways_inverse` at position -i gives column X (-(i+1)) s = column X (-i) (s + 1) XOR (column X (-i) s || column X (-(i-1)) s), and the same for Y; XOR-ing, D (i+1) s is false as soon as D i (s+1), D i s and D (i-1) s are, and the triangle's index arithmetic supplies all three. Reading the claim at s = t needs exactly i ≤ j.

WHERE THE WORK IS. The induction is two-step — the case i + 1 needs both i and i - 1 — so it wants `Nat.strong_induction_on` or a paired invariant rather than plain `induction i`. The triangle bound is the other half: carrying `∀ s, t ≤ s → s + i ≤ t + j → ...` rather than a statement at the single time t is what makes the step go through.

WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT. It is the quantitative form of the shielding the mask law shows at one column. Read with Y the picture grown from row p, it says: if the centre column repeats at lag p and has a run of j consecutive black cells at time t, then the j columns to the left of the origin all repeat at lag p at that time. So a proof that a repeating centre column forces a repeating neighbour cannot come from the black cells — it has to come from what happens between the runs. That is where the difficulty actually lives, and the board has never said so in a theorem.
proposals.disclaims: `i ≤ j` is exact, not an artefact of the proof: the next position along genuinely differs. Over random configuration pairs the two pictures differ at position -(j+1) in 17,596 of 311,892 hypothesis hits (explorer/seeder_p1_runshield.mjs), and 7 times inside the witness's own range (explorer/seeder_p1_live.lean). So there is no stronger version to reach for. This is a statement about black runs only and says nothing about the times between them, which is precisely the open part.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_periodic_damage_white (p N : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t) (M : ℕ) :
    ∃ t ≥ M, centerColumn t = false ∧ evolve (t + p) (-1) ≠ evolve t (-1) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason:
If the centre column repeated with period p, then it would have infinitely many white cells at which its left neighbour fails to repeat with that same period. This is a consequence of the prize conjecture's negation — a step inside a proof by contradiction, in the same shape as the board's `centerColumn_other_of_cohomologous_column`, which also takes the periodicity as a hypothesis.

WHY IT IS TRUE. Suppose not: some M has no such t. Set K = max M N. For every t ≥ K the left neighbour repeats at lag p, for one of two reasons. At a WHITE cell of the centre column, that is the failed assumption. At a BLACK cell it is free: `centerColumn_succ_of_black` at t gives evolve t (-1) = !centerColumn (t + 1), and hc turns centerColumn t = true into centerColumn (t + p) = true, so the same lemma at t + p gives evolve (t + p) (-1) = !centerColumn (t + p + 1), and hc again makes centerColumn (t + p + 1) = centerColumn (t + 1). The two are equal. So column -1 is p-periodic from K, and the centre column is p-periodic from N, so columns -1 and 0 are both eventually periodic — which `not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent (-1)` forbids. (`-1 + 1` needs one `norm_num` to be seen as 0, and centerColumn is `fun t => evolve t 0` definitionally.)

WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT. A proof of either P1 wall assumes the centre column repeats and derives a contradiction. Ask what such a proof has to work with today and the honest answer is Jen's theorem and nothing else — Jen is a single negative fact, and no node turns it into anything a later step can use. This does: it converts Jen into a specific infinite set of times, the white cells at which the left neighbour breaks step, and those are exactly the times the mask law in this tier is about (at a black cell the mask is closed, so nothing can happen there). Together the two say where a contradiction must be found, which is more than the board says now.
proposals.disclaims: The hypothesis is the negation of Prize 1, so nobody can exhibit a p and N satisfying it and the statement carries no witness — a finite range would only confirm that the hypothesis is unsatisfiable there, which is not what is claimed. It is NOT the wall and does not weaken it: it is one consequence a proof of the wall would derive, not a sufficient condition for it. Nothing here rules the hypothesis out; if it could, it would be the prize.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_eq_evolve_mul_pow (k m : ℕ) :
    evolve (m * 2 ^ k + k) ((m * 2 ^ k : ℕ) : ℤ) = centerColumn k := by
  sorry
proposals.reason:
The centre column reappears verbatim, arbitrarily far out on the right: the cell at position m * 2^k after m * 2^k + k steps is the centre column's k-th cell, for every m.

WHY IT IS TRUE. `rightDiagonal k j` is `evolve (j + k) j` by definition, so the statement is `rightDiagonal k (m * 2 ^ k) = rightDiagonal k 0` once `0 + k = k` is simplified. And `rightDiagonal_periodicFrom_pow` says `rightDiagonal k` is periodic with period 2^k from index 0 — exactly, with no onset and no transient — so `periodicFrom_mul` gives period m * 2^k from index 0, and reading that at n = 0 is the whole proof. The m = 0 case is the trivial one and is not vacuous cover: every m ≥ 1 is real content.

WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT. Nothing on the board relates the centre column to any cell away from the origin, and crystal 70 asks for exactly this as the opening move of the right-side route. The left-hand twin, `leftDiagonal_mul_pow_eq_settledCenter`, lands on `settledCenter`, a DIFFERENT sequence, because the left diagonals have transients and index 0 sits inside one; the right diagonals have none, so the same argument lands on the centre column itself. That difference is the whole of crystal 70's claim that the right side is a better position, and this makes it a theorem instead of a remark. Concretely it is a transfer principle: any statement about the cells (m * 2^k + k, m * 2^k), where the right-diagonal machinery is exact, is a statement about the centre column.
proposals.disclaims: This is infrastructure, not an attack: by itself it proves nothing about either wall, and it is a short consequence of two closed nodes. It also does not touch obstruction 69's ratio — the centre column still outruns the left-hand settling front, and this says nothing about that. Its value is that it is the first node putting the centre column anywhere but the origin.

witness.range: the pairs (k, m) listed, so k ≤ 3 and m ≤ 3, the deepest being k = 3, m = 1 — cell 8 of row 11. Evaluated true by `lake env lean` at seed time (explorer/seeder_p1_final.lean). The list is explicit rather than a range because the cost is 3^(m * 2^k + k): k = 2, m = 3 is row 15 and already 14 million neighbour evaluations, and k = 3, m = 2 is row 19 and out of reach. Independently checked to k ≤ 6, m ≤ 4 — 35 pairs, 0 failures — with the array engine (explorer/seeder_p1_damage.mjs).
